FINAL_STATES is present, nonempty, and u2 is declared in STATES and serves as the accepting terminal (exit reached); the header is not omitted. Reachability: u0 is initial, u1 is reached via switch_toggled, and u2 is reachable from both u0 and u1 via at_exit, so no dead states. Compactness: 3 states is minimal — a separate u1 is needed to make the toggle bonus one-shot (no re-farming of 0.1 on repeated toggles, since (u1, else) self-loops at 0), and u2 is the absorbing terminal. Predicate/event discipline: transitions use only real propositions — switch_toggled (a genuine one-step event, correct for 'flip the switch', and correctly rewarded on every toggle including a silent siren, which is just 'flipping the switch') and at_exit (terminal-only condition); no invented predicates like 'siren_off' or 'at_switch'. Irrelevant events (siren_ringing changes, holding_box, box_fell) are all absorbed by the per-state else self-loops, as required. Constraint compatibility: switch_toggled and at_exit can never co-occur per the environment constraints, so the ordering of the two u0 transitions is safe. No regression states are needed: the task imposes no maintained condition at exit (unlike 'siren silent' or 'holding box' variants), so u1 absorbing apart from exit is correct, not a fidelity gap. Implicit zero rewards on the else self-loops are acceptable; an explicit (u1, switch_toggled, u1) -> 0.0 entry would be redundant since else covers it. Minor nit only: listing the self-loop rewards explicitly would improve auditability, but it does not affect acceptance.
